 Poland and Sweden meet in the final round of the 2026-27 UEFA Nations League group stage on Tuesday, 17 November, at 19:45 (UK time). The match takes place at Tarczynski Arena in Wroclaw, with the hosts fighting to avoid automatic relegation from League B.
 Sweden have already secured promotion to League A after an unbeaten campaign, while Poland sit third in Group B4 with just four points. The visitors won the reverse fixture 3-1 in September, but the Eagles will be hoping to take advantage of their home record to secure a crucial result.

 Poland vs. Sweden - Head-to-head record
 Sweden have historically enjoyed the better of their meetings with Poland, winning 11 of the 15 encounters. Poland have recorded three victories, while one match ended in a draw.
 The visitors have also dominated more recent meetings , winning eight of the last nine encounters between the two nations. Their latest victory came in September, when Sweden secured a 3-1 home win in the Nations League.
 Poland’s most notable recent success came in March 2022, when they beat Sweden 2-0 in a World Cup qualifying playoff. However, the Swedes have since won both meetings, including a 3-2 victory in March 2026.
 Despite that historical disadvantage, Poland will be hoping to make home advantage count in a match that could determine their League B survival.

 Poland - Relying on home advantage
 Poland enter their final Nations League fixture under considerable pressure after losing three of their last four matches. With automatic relegation still a possibility, let’s examine their recent performances and expected line-up.
 Recent form
 Poland have endured a difficult Group B4 campaign, collecting just four points from their opening five matches . Jan Urban’s side began with a goalless home draw against Bosnia and Herzegovina before losing 3-1 away to Sweden, although they responded with an emphatic 6-0 victory over Romania.
 However, consecutive away defeats have left the Eagles in a precarious position. Poland lost 1-0 to Bosnia and Herzegovina in October before suffering a 2-1 defeat against Romania on Saturday, missing the opportunity to secure a place in the League B/C relegation playoffs.
 Those results leave Poland third in the group, just one point ahead of bottom-placed Romania. A victory over Sweden would guarantee they avoid automatic relegation, while anything less could leave them dependent on Romania’s result against Bosnia and Herzegovina.
 Urban faces several selection problems ahead of this crucial fixture. Jakub Kiwior is suspended, Matty Cash is doubtful with a leg injury, and goalkeeper Kamil Grabara remains sidelined with a cruciate ligament injury. Piotr Zielinski is also unavailable through illness, while Robert Lewandowski is expected to lead the attack alongside Karol Swiderski.

 Sweden – Looking to finish unbeaten
 Let’s look at Sweden’s current situation. We will analyse their impressive form, recent results, and key players to watch in this upcoming match.
 Recent form
 Sweden have collected 13 points from five Nations League matches, recording four victories and one draw. They began their campaign with consecutive home wins over Romania and Poland before drawing 1-1 away to Bosnia and Herzegovina.
 The Blue and Yellow returned to winning ways with a 1-0 victory away to Romania before securing a dramatic 3-2 home success against Bosnia and Herzegovina on Saturday. That victory confirmed Sweden’s position at the top of Group B4, five points ahead of second-placed Bosnia and Herzegovina.
 Potter’s side have been particularly effective in attack , scoring in the opening 20 minutes of six of their last seven Nations League matches. However, defensive vulnerabilities remain, with both teams scoring in 13 of their last 15 fixtures across all competitions.
 Sweden will be without Lucas Bergvall, who has a knee injury, and Patrik Walemark, who is sidelined with a muscle problem. Hugo Larsson and Yasin Ayari are expected to feature in midfield, while Anthony Elanga and Sebastian Nanasi could provide width. Viktor Gyokeres should partner Alexander Isak in attack.

 Predictions for Poland vs. Sweden - Visitors' Form to Prevail
 Sweden have been particularly effective in the opening stages of their recent matches, scoring early in six of their last seven Nations League fixtures. With Gyokeres and Isak expected to lead the attack, over 0.5 goals in the first half is an appealing option.
 Poland need a positive result to protect their position in League B, while Sweden will be looking to complete their unbeaten campaign with another victory. Both sides have attacking quality, making the match not to end in a draw another market worth considering.
 Despite Sweden’s impressive form, Poland have remained unbeaten at home throughout the competition. With the visitors already guaranteed promotion, the hosts could take advantage.
